ayuda.directivas.rp5: «.include "file.s"» inserts another file (the program must be saved to disk); «.eqv NAME value» defines constants; «.macro name (%p)…/.end_macro» defines macros; «%hi(x)»/«%lo(x)» split an address for «lui»+«addi». Details: docs/ENSAMBLADOR.md §4.4.
ayuda.atomicas: Advanced extensions: A (atomics — amoadd.w, lr.w/sc.w and family, 4 bytes; EmuRV is single-hart, so sc always succeeds: they are for learning the pattern, not real concurrency) and C (compressed — c.addi, c.li, c.mv, c.lw… 2 bytes; the assembler does not compress on its own, you write them by hand). The «Atomics and compressed» example shows them; details in docs/ENSAMBLADOR.md §4.1.
ayuda.flotantes: Floating point (RV32F/D): registers f0–f31 with ABI names (ft, fs, fa); .s (single) and .d (double) arithmetic, conversions, comparisons and fma. The values appear in the collapsible «F registers (floating point)» panel (64-bit hex + interpreted number). The «Floating point» example shows it; details in docs/ENSAMBLADOR.md §4.1.
ayuda.traps: Advanced: with «csrw mtvec, reg» the program installs its own exception handler — unknown ecalls, illegal instructions and invalid accesses jump there (mcause says what happened) and «mret» returns. The «Exception handler» example shows it in full; details in docs/TRAPS.md.
ayuda.ebreak: Also, the «ebreak» instruction pauses the program (a software pause, like a breakpoint set from code): you can inspect registers and memory, and resume with «Run» or «Step» from the next instruction.

ayuda.temas.texto: Use the theme selector in the toolbar to pick the look. There are five: «Educational» (sober dark, default), «Retro-CRT» (amber phosphor with scanlines), «Parchment» (warm light paper), «Retro Kawaii» (vaporwave pastel) and «Floppy 90s» (90s desktop beige). The change applies instantly, is remembered, and also recolors the editor syntax. All five keep good contrast (WCAG AA) so the code stays comfortable to read.
ayuda.idioma.texto: EmuRV is available in Spanish or English: use the ES/EN selector in the toolbar (your choice is remembered). The translation covers the interface; the assembler error messages and the lessons stay in Spanish even in English mode — they are the project’s teaching material.
ayuda.ciclo.texto: Write your program, press «Assemble» and then «Run» (runs to the end) or «Step» (one instruction at a time). «Reset» returns the machine to its initial state without re-assembling. The panels on the right show the registers (changed ones are highlighted) and memory. With the ⧉ button in its header, each panel opens in its own window (it returns when you close it). For your files: «New» starts a blank program, «Open» loads one from disk, «Save» writes it (the first time it asks where; after that it saves there directly) and «Save as» picks another location.
ayuda.binario: «Open» also accepts RISC-V ELF32 executables: the editor shows the disassembled listing (read-only) and Run/Step/breakpoints work on the listing. To compile with gcc: -march=rv32im -mabi=ilp32 -Ttext=0x00400000 -Tdata=0x10010000 -nostdlib (details: README §Open binaries).
ayuda.lecciones: Starting from scratch? Press the «Lessons» button in the toolbar: a two-column modal with the 10-lesson course and your progress. Picking one shows its objectives and which panels to watch before opening it; «Open lesson» loads the code into the editor to step through it. Your progress (completed lessons) is remembered. Lesson 8 uses several files: opening it asks for a folder to save them (the .include needs it).
ayuda.syscalls.texto: Load the service number into a7, the arguments into a0, and run «ecall»:
ayuda.syscalls.s5: read integer (the console waits for your input)
ayuda.syscalls.s8: read string: stores at most a1−1 characters + trailing 0 byte (truncates without error)
ayuda.syscalls.s9: allocate heap memory (sbrk; starts at 0x10040000, no free)
ayuda.syscalls.s32: sleep: pauses the program for a0 milliseconds
ayuda.syscalls.s60: clear the console (EmuRV extension — not in RARS)
ayuda.syscalls.s93: exit with a status code (the CLI propagates it to the shell, clamped to 0..125)
ayuda.teclado.texto: The keyboard is a memory-mapped device (MMIO), like in RARS/MARS: the program polls it by reading two words. Bit 1 of the control register is reserved (always 0). To type: click the panel's screen (it keeps capturing until you click outside) or any key with the separate screen window in front.
ayuda.teclado.control: RECEIVER_CONTROL — bit 0 set to 1 if a key is pending (bit 1 reserved)
ayuda.teclado.dato: RECEIVER_DATA — code of the oldest key; reading it consumes it from the queue
ayuda.memoria.sp: top of the stack (initial sp; grows downward)
ayuda.ejemplos.texto: The «Examples» menu loads commented programs: hello world, interactive sum, counter, fibonacci, stack/functions (recursive factorial), color stripes and graphical Tetris (a port of an 8086 Tetris, drawn on the 320×240 screen), keyboard echo and real-time Tetris (MMIO keyboard), exception handler (CSRs/traps) and floating point (grade average with F/D). They are a good starting point for your own code.
ayuda.editor.texto: The editor helps you as you write: autocompletion of mnemonics, registers and labels (appears as you type, or with Ctrl-Space); hovering over an instruction shows its syntax and what it does; Cmd/Ctrl-click on a label jumps to its definition, and placing the cursor on a label highlights all its uses. Errors still show up when you «Assemble» (the editor does not re-assemble while you type).
ayuda.depuracion.texto: The «Debug» panel starts collapsed (it's for later) and opens on its own once you set your first breakpoint. There you can add a condition to each one (e.g. «t0 == 5»: stops only when it holds) and, in the collapsible «Watchpoints» sub-section (with a short help note when you open it), watch data regions (they stop when the program reads or writes them). With the machine paused, double-click a register or a memory word to edit it live. Details: docs/DEPURACION.md.
ayuda.breakpoints.texto: Click the editor's left gutter (to the left of the line number) to add or remove a red dot. «Run» stops when it reaches that line, before executing it; the line is highlighted and you can inspect registers and memory, continue with «Step» or resume with «Run».

ayuda.memoria.buscar: To find a value, use the Memory panel's search box: pick the type (hex byte, hex word or ASCII text), type the value and «Search». A word is searched exactly as stored in memory (little-endian: the word 0x0000002A is located as the bytes 2A 00 00 00). The ‹ and › buttons jump to the previous and next match (also with Enter and Shift+Enter). The search scans the data region (.data, .bss and the heap).

ayuda.temas.usuario: You can also build your own theme: «Edit theme» (next to the selector) opens an editor with a color control for each element (backgrounds, text, accent, states and the editor syntax). Changes preview live, are saved on your device and show up as «Custom» in the selector. If a color ends up with low contrast for reading, the editor warns you (it does not block you: it's your theme). You can return to the starting point with «Reset to Educational», and export or import your theme as a JSON file.
